parties:
Shefalika Khisa and others………..Petitioners
vs
Chairman, Land Appeal Board and others……..Respondents
full_judgment: 13. On a plain reading of the aforesaid provisions, it is crystal clear that the Government can only revise the order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner and thereby Land Appeal Board has no jurisdiction to adjudicate the order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner relating to civil dispute of the tribes under the Regulations, 1900 and that this legal proposition has also been settled in the case of Wagachara Tea Estate Ltd vs Md Abu Taher reported in 69 DLR (AD) 381; wherein the apex Court held as under: "In the present case, the High Court Division rightly held that the language of the circular under memo dated 23rd May, 1989, does not show that the Land Appeal Board has been given power to hear appeal or revision in respect of matters arising out of civil suits disposed of by the Deputy Commissioner of CHT; that the Land Appeal Board Rules do not show that it has jurisdiction to hear appeal or revision in matters arising out of civil suit disposed of by the Deputy Commissioner of the Hill districts and that section 17(3) of the section of 1900 has not delegated the powers of the government to the Land Appeal Board. However, the observations that in Bikram Kishore Chakma (6 BLC 436), it was out of a dispute over "settlement of government khas land within Chittagong Hill District" meaning thereby that in case of disputes over settlement of land of the three hill districts, the Board has power to revise any decision given by the Commissioner is not a sound view in view of sub-section (3) of section 17 which clearly provides that the government may 'revise any order made under this sections. It is only the government which can revise any decision of the Commissioner made in exercise of power under Regulations, 1900. The Board has no power to decide any dispute from the decision of the Commissioner over the settlement of government khas land or any other matters relating to vested and Non-resident Property, Abandoned Property, Land Survey Record, Land Development Tax, Certificate Case, Waqf or Debuttor property or any other related matters which cover Regulations of 1900."
